Chapter 7: The Father’s Heart and the Hearts of Jesus and Mary
As your devotion grows, you might find yourself wondering—how does the Father’s Heart fit with the Sacred Heart of Jesus and the Immaculate Heart of Mary? Maybe you’ve even worried that turning your heart toward the Father means leaving Jesus or Mary behind.
But here’s the beautiful truth: these three Hearts aren’t in competition. They’re companions—like a family gathered around the same table, each with their own personality and role, but all held together by love.
Picture it for a moment. The Father’s Heart, the Heart of Jesus, and the Heart of Mary—they form a spiritual family. Each reveals a unique side of God’s love. If you’ve always found comfort in the Sacred Heart of Jesus, opening your heart to the Father isn’t about stepping away from Jesus. It’s more like going deeper, discovering that the love you see in Jesus is the very love of the Father, poured out without holding back.
Think about the wounds in Jesus’ Heart. They’re not just His—they’re the wounds of the Father’s Heart too. It’s a love that suffers for you, that gives everything, that never stops hoping.
And Mary? Her Heart is right there in this mystery. Her gentleness, her faith, her “yes”—all of that is a reflection of the Father’s own love. There’s a story about a woman who’d prayed to Mary for years. Suddenly she felt drawn to the Father’s Heart, and at first, she was worried—was she leaving Mary behind? But in prayer, she realized Mary was actually leading her closer to the Father, guiding her to the very source of love.
These stories and prayers show how the three devotions don’t pull you apart. They lift you up together. When your heart aches, Mary brings comfort. When you’re struggling, Jesus offers strength. And when fear creeps in, the Father gives you security. It’s like a trinity of love, each Heart opening another doorway deeper into God’s mystery.
Most people never realize how much the Father delights in being known and loved right alongside Jesus and Mary. So, next time you pray, try making room for all three Hearts. Each has something special to offer. Devotion to the Father’s Heart doesn’t replace the others—it completes them. It’s a way of joining the whole family of God, stepping into the fullness of love that’s been waiting for you all along.
